claim: For every finite family of orthonormal bases \(\mathcal B^{(1)},\ldots,\mathcal B^{(m)}\) of the real Hilbert space \(\ell_2\), there is a uniformly bounded sequence of rank-one operators \(T_n:\ell_2	o c_0\) such that each tested union \( igcup_{n,k}T_n b_k^{(j)}\) is relatively compact, while \( igcup_n T_n(B_{\ell_2})\) is not limited. Thus no finite list of orthonormal-basis tests certifies collective limitedness, even for rank-one operators.
scientific_limitations_and_integrity: The proof is analytic and applies to every finite prescribed family of bases in real ell_2. It does not address infinite testing families or other possible criteria. Self-review only; independent audit and independent validation have not been performed. Literature-priority risk remains.
title: No finite basis test certifies collective limitedness
